tasks.short: Chart teeth during the exam, write the treatment note, have the dentist sign it, file it, enter treatment codes and record material batches.

steps.what: Assistant charts teeth and surfaces as the dentist calls them out
Assistant types the treatment information into the patient record after the treatment

loop.input: The recording of the treatment talk, made only with the patient's consent, and the practice's fixed note template.
loop.output: A draft treatment note in the template: anaesthetic, materials, findings and advice.
loop.check: Every drug name and dose must match the practice's medicines list and appear in the transcript; every number must appear in the transcript; the assistant corrects the draft and it goes to the dentist; nothing enters the record unsigned.
loop.stop: One draft per treatment; without consent or on failure the assistant types the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: The treatment talk is free speech; a template alone cannot turn it into a note.

steps.what: Dentist checks and signs the treatment note
Assistant saves the note to the patient's dossier
Assistant looks up and enters treatment codes for the bill
Assistant types the batch numbers of materials used

tasks.design: With the patient's consent, a CE-marked scribe in the dental record system ({OTHER}) drafts the treatment note from the treatment talk into the practice template, with drug names and numbers checked against lists and the transcript; the assistant corrects it, the dentist signs, and only then does the system save it to the dossier. Treatment codes are proposed from the charted treatments for the assistant to check, and batch labels are scanned; charting stays live.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed after each treatment and codes looked up by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Dutch practices use ambient scribes that draft consult notes for the clinician to approve; record systems can map charted treatments to tariff codes.
tasks.still_hard: Scribes make verified errors in a share of notes; patients may hold back with a recorder on; the scribe must be CE-marked class IIa or higher.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what the dentist meant, not only what they said, and getting it right in the record.
tasks.altitude: The assistant corrects drafts and checks codes; the dentist still signs every note.

reach.learn: Whether the same template and checks suit hygiene treatments.

evidence.claim: A Dutch ambient scribe drafts the consult note for the clinician to approve and is used in many GP practices.
In a study of 12 Dutch GPs, an ambient scribe cut documentation time by 42.7 seconds per consult; total consult time did not change.
A preprint found verified errors in 31.3% of 565 notes from three deployed scribes.
A regulator found class I not compatible for a scribe whose notes feed continued care; class IIa is the floor.
The dossier is kept 20 years and shared only with consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from charting to the filed note, codes and batches; billing is outside.
Input contract: recording consent asked by the assistant at the start; note template and medicines list kept by the practice owner; code mapping from the record system supplier; fallback is typing.
Recordings are deleted once the note is signed.
Dentist time is outside the assistant's savings.
unknowns: Share of patients who consent to recording.
research_questions: How often does the dentist change the corrected draft?

incremental.description: Assistant asks for recording consent and handles refusals.
Practice owner audits samples of signed notes.

approvals.approved_version: The treatment note as signed by the dentist in s3; any later edit needs a new signature.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Patients who refuse recording and complex treatments keep notes typed by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Track stock with empty-bin cards, build and check the order, get large orders approved, send them, unpack deliveries and keep equipment service dates.

steps.what: Assistant counts dental supplies in the cupboards and writes a stock list
Assistant works out what to order from the stock list
Assistant decides quantities and adds special items to the order
Practice manager approves orders above the budget limit
Assistant places the order in the supplier's webshop
Assistant unpacks deliveries and checks them against the order
Assistant keeps equipment service dates on a wall chart and checks it
Assistant phones the service company to book equipment maintenance

tasks.design: Supplies sit in two bins with a barcode card; the assistant scans the card when a bin empties, which replaces the weekly count. The practice management system ({OTHER}) turns scans and minimum levels into a proposed order, the assistant adjusts it, the practice manager approves orders above the limit, and the system sends the order to the supplier's webshop. An equipment register raises an alert when a service is due; unpacking and booking the service visit stay manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock was counted by eye and orders typed into the webshop; service dates sat on a wall chart.
tasks.enabler_now: Barcode two-bin systems and supplier webshop links are standard; registers can alert on dates.
tasks.still_hard: Cards get lost; expiry dates of materials still need checking.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a new dentist uses a different composite and changing the order.
tasks.altitude: The assistant checks proposed orders; spending approval stays with the practice manager.

evidence.claim: Barcode two-bin cards and supplier webshop links support automatic reorder proposals.
Medical devices in the practice must be maintained per the maker's instructions.

assumptions: Boundary: from stock signals to stocked supplies and booked services; paying invoices is outside.

Input contract: minimum levels and cards set by the head assistant; budget limit set by the practice manager; equipment register with service intervals kept by the practice manager; fallback is counting and the wall chart.
Manager time is outside the assistant's savings.
Unpacking and booking visits do not change.
unknowns: Whether the supplier accepts system orders.

approvals.approved_version: The order lines and total as approved by the practice manager in s4; orders under the limit follow the checked order; any change above the limit needs a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Small practices with few items save less on counting.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain aftercare to the patient, add the dentist's extra instructions, check the leaflet fits the treatment, send it, and answer patients' calls afterwards.

steps.what: Assistant explains postoperative care to the patient after treatment
Assistant writes the dentist's extra instructions on the leaflet by hand
Assistant finds the right printed leaflet for the treatment and checks it
Assistant hands the patient the leaflet with the instructions prescribed by the dentist
Assistant answers patients' phone questions after treatment

tasks.design: Fixed aftercare templates per treatment, approved once by the dentist, sit in the dental record system ({OTHER}) and are chosen from the charted treatment; the assistant types any extra instructions into a field and checks the sheet. Once the assistant marks it checked, the system prints it and sends it to the patient's portal. Explaining aftercare and answering calls stay in person and by phone; no phone bot is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leaflets were picked from a drawer and extra instructions handwritten.
tasks.enabler_now: Record systems can select templates from treatment codes and send them to patient portals.
tasks.still_hard: Templates must match what the dentist prescribes; patients still need the explanation.
tasks.human_edge: Making sure a numb, anxious patient actually understands what to do tonight.

reach.learn: Whether portal copies reduce evening calls.

evidence.claim: Post-operative instructions can come from fixed templates per treatment.
Health data in the portal is special-category data under professional secrecy.
A phone bot must tell callers they speak to AI; this design has none.

assumptions: Boundary: from the end of treatment to questions afterwards; complications needing the dentist are outside.
Input contract: templates per treatment written and approved by the dentist; patient portal from the record system supplier; fallback is printed leaflets.
Explaining and answering calls do not change.
Patients without a portal get the printout only.
unknowns: Share of patients using the portal.
research_questions: Do patients follow aftercare better with a portal copy?

incremental.description: Assistant types extra instructions into the template field.

approvals.approved_version: The aftercare sheet with extra instructions as checked by the assistant in s3; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is explaining in person and answering calls.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Show brushing and flossing, disclose plaque, record plaque scores, write a home-care plan, give it to the patient and set the recall.

steps.what: Assistant instructs patients in brushing and flossing technique
Assistant stains plaque and shows the patient where it builds up
Assistant records plaque control scores on a paper chart
Assistant writes a home-care plan for the patient
Assistant hands the patient a copy of the plan
Assistant writes the next check-up date on an appointment card

tasks.design: Plaque scores are clicked per tooth surface in the dental record system ({OTHER}), which builds a home-care plan from a template marking the problem areas for the assistant to check; once checked, the system prints it and sends it to the patient's portal. The recall date is set from the scores and a reminder is sent; instructing and showing stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scores were on paper charts and plans were handwritten.
tasks.enabler_now: Dental record systems hold plaque indices per surface and send recall reminders.
tasks.still_hard: Changing a patient's habits is a conversation; a printed plan does little on its own.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the words that make a teenager actually floss.

reach.learn: Whether stored scores show progress patients can see.

evidence.claim: Dental record systems hold plaque indices per tooth surface and send recall reminders.
Plaque scores are health data kept in the dossier under professional secrecy.

assumptions: Boundary: from instruction to the recall set; the hygienist's treatment is outside.
Input contract: plan template and recall rules set by the dentist; fallback is paper charts and cards.
Instructing and showing do not change.
Patients without a portal get the printout.
research_questions: Do plaque scores improve more when patients see their history?

already_counted.description: Assistant checks the built home-care plan.

incremental.description: Assistant learns the plaque score screen.

approvals.approved_version: The home-care plan as checked by the assistant in s4; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is instruction in the chair.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The dental assistant keeps chairside work, patient instruction and judgement; typing notes, counting stock and handwriting sheets shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An assistant who spends the day with patients while records, orders and reminders keep themselves.
